game.title: Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs

lede: Denver Broncos carries the stronger EdgeDesk offensive profile (#14 in EPA per play) and the better defensive rating with it, so the ratings point the same way on both sides of the ball.
EdgeDesk’s independent projection makes it Kansas City Chiefs +2.6 with a fair total of 39.3 — approximately a one-score game, before any sportsbook number is consulted.

The widest measured matchup on the board is Kansas City Chiefs pass offence vs Denver Broncos pass defence, which sits −0.254 from the league mean once the two ratings are combined the way the model combines them.
The largest uncertainty is availability: NFL injury report — not loaded in this session.

score.note: Split from EdgeDesk’s own fair spread and fair total, rounded to whole points. It is the centre of a distribution, not a prediction of the exact score.

moneyline.note: EdgeDesk’s own fair price, with no margin in it. It is not a quote and nobody offers it.

outcome_range.note: Quoted from the perspective of Kansas City Chiefs, off the engine’s own learned margin distribution (conditioned on this spread, so real key-number mass is kept). Eight results in ten land inside p10–p90.

projection.confidence_absent_reason: The NFL model publishes no single confidence score. What it publishes instead is the width of the outcome range above and the sample the ratings rest on: the trained seeds through 2025, plus 2 absorbed 2026 games.
projection.status_note: EdgeDesk differs from the market by 5.1 points. That is enough to look harder — and out of sample no gap size of any width has cleared p<0.05 against the close, so it is a research prompt and not an edge.
projection.validation: UNPROVEN — this model does NOT beat the closing line out of sample. Research only; nothing here is graded as a bet.
